design_principles: Two MCPs: Jurisdiction (public data) and Personal (user context)
User context stored in Personal MCP (localStorage/IndexedDB), never sent to Jurisdiction MCP
Personal MCP queries Jurisdiction MCP, applies filtering, explains relevance
No query logging, no behavior tracking, no engagement metrics
Transparent reasoning: agent explains why it surfaced something
User controls keys: Nostr signing always happens client-side in Personal MCP
City attestation is additive (trust signal), not gate-keeping (permissionless relay)

architectural_decisions.title: Extension IS the Personal MCP
architectural_decisions.context: The edge intelligence architecture originally planned apps/civicos-personal-mcp/ as a separate Python/TypeScript package. Meanwhile, the browser extension grew to contain identity management (passkey, wallet, signing), user context (stances, follows), relay connection (voice, comments, coordination), BYOK AI (inline chat), and Jurisdiction MCP queries. The extension already IS the Personal MCP.
architectural_decisions.decision: Consolidate Personal MCP into the browser extension. Do not build apps/civicos-personal-mcp/ as a separate runtime. Identity providers and signing code already ported to extension (lib/providers/). Future Personal MCP tools (get_suggestions, get_relevant_now) should be built as extension internal APIs.
architectural_decisions.consequences: Simplifies architecture (no separate package to deploy/maintain). Extension becomes the canonical edge agent runtime. WebMCP (Chrome 146+, mid-to-late 2026) can later expose extension tools to AI agents natively via ExtensionServerTransport.

architectural_decisions.title: Structure extension APIs as tool-shaped for WebMCP readiness
architectural_decisions.context: WebMCP (W3C, Google/Microsoft initiative) ships in Chrome 146 early preview (Feb 2026, behind flag). ExtensionServerTransport allows extensions to expose themselves as MCP servers to AI agents in the browser. Production readiness expected mid-to-late 2026.
architectural_decisions.decision: Structure extension internal functions (castVoice, getMyActivity, getSuggestions, etc.) as clean, tool-shaped APIs with typed inputs/outputs. This is good practice regardless and makes future WebMCP exposure trivial. Do NOT depend on WebMCP for pilot — it is behind a flag and not production-ready.
architectural_decisions.consequences: When WebMCP stabilizes, the extension can expose its tools to Claude.ai/Gemini/etc. natively, completing the edge intelligence vision without a separate server process. Zero additional install for users.

architectural_decisions.title: Keep Jurisdiction MCP unauthenticated; OAuth only for federation
architectural_decisions.context: MCP OAuth 2.1 spec standardized (March 2025, updated June 2025). The two-MCP architecture intentionally keeps Jurisdiction MCP anonymous — it serves public civic data and does not know who is asking. This is a privacy feature, not a limitation.
architectural_decisions.decision: Do NOT add MCP OAuth to the Jurisdiction MCP for user-level authentication. The Jurisdiction MCP remains unauthenticated for reads (public data). Write operations go through the relay with Nostr signatures (cryptographic, not OAuth). Reserve OAuth for multi-jurisdiction federation: when a Marin County MCP needs to verify 'this request comes from an authorized San Rafael instance' (jurisdiction-level, not user-level auth).
architectural_decisions.consequences: Preserves privacy boundary (no user tracking at the MCP layer). Simplifies connector setup (no OAuth consent flow). Federation auth is a post-pilot concern for multi-jurisdiction expansion.

technical_considerations: Svelte customElement option compiles to Web Components (Shadow DOM)
Shadow DOM scopes CSS — must bundle styles with component, not rely on global styles
Props passed as attributes (strings) — complex objects need JSON serialization or property access
Cross-component state via CustomEvents (bubbling) — no shared store in Shadow DOM
Extension can import components directly (same bundler) — external surfaces use <script> tag
